patch.summary: MailerLite cost guide: researched plan structure, free/trial flags, who each tier suits, cost scenarios, and value tradeoffs — no invented prices.

blocks.body: MailerLite pricing is plan-gated across 4 researched tiers. Free entry: Free. Trial/free path present in researched plans. Compare seat/capacity gates and unlocks — not list-price folklore.

blocks.heading: MailerLite cost scenarios to pressure-test
blocks.body: Price MailerLite against how you actually buy seats and unlocks — not against a competitor's homepage headline.

scenarios.title: Lean team / free-or-trial first
scenarios.body: Stay on Free until a gated capability (premium unlock) becomes mandatory.

scenarios.title: Growing team with gated workflows
scenarios.body: Map must-have workflows (email campaigns, newsletter builder, email templates) to plan unlocks before expanding seats.

scenarios.title: Hidden / extra cost watch
scenarios.body: Budget risk: Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days. Also check add-ons, overages, and admin time outside the sticker plan.

steps.label: Pay up when SMBs and creators wanting simple email with a free starting rung requires a paid unlock you will use weekly
Do not overbuy if this limitation dominates: Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days

items.body: Free caps at 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per 30 days

items.title: Cost trap 2
items.body: Automation and segmentation depth trail Klaviyo and ActiveCampaign

items.title: Cost trap 3
items.body: Plan rename (Comfort/Power) may confuse older comparison content — use new names

items.title: Cost trap 4
items.body: AI assistance is lighter than AI-forward ESP peers

items.title: Cost trap 5
items.body: Not ideal for complex B2B multi-product marketing automation / CRM-heavy stacks
